STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel is a square white flat plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall, so it is a flat plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are usually 20-30 cm. This one looks medium, around 24 cm across.
b) Reference: the plate spans about 2.2 fork lengths across the width, which gives about 21-23 cm (fork 19 cm).
Reconciled width: about 23 cm, so the area is about 529 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Bacon strips (cooked, crisp): three to four strips lying over the centre-left. Footprint about 12% of the plate, roughly 63 cm². Thickness about 0.5 cm (two layers of strip). Volume about 32 ml. Bacon is roughly 1.0 g/ml, so about 35 g.
- Mashed potato (the white mound on the right): footprint about 25% of the plate, roughly 130 cm². Mound averages about 2 cm thick (peak about 4 cm). Volume about 260 ml × 1.0 = about 200 g (mash is about 1.0 g/ml, so roughly 210 g).
- Cooked spinach: a small bed under the bacon and beside the mash, about 8% of the plate, roughly 40 cm², with about 1 cm average thickness. Volume about 40 ml × 0.6 = about 25 g.
- Shredded carrot: a few strands, about 2% of the plate, roughly 10 cm², about 0.5 cm thick. Volume about 5 ml × 0.6 = about 3 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer beyond the greens under the bacon. No extra items added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Bacon, cooked: about 540 kcal/100 g
- Mashed potato (with butter/milk): about 110 kcal/100 g
- Cooked spinach: about 25 kcal/100 g
- Carrot, raw/shredded: about 40 kcal/100 g

Totals: about 35 g bacon (about 190 kcal), about 210 g mash (about 230 kcal), about 25 g spinach (about 6 kcal), about 3 g carrot (about 1 kcal). Total about 273 g and about 430 kcal.
